class.name: Box3DCollision
class.brief_description: Upstream's standalone collision queries: rays, sweeps, overlaps, distance, time of impact and manifolds, on geometry that is in no world.
class.description: Static collision maths on raw geometry. Every call is [b]static and needs no world[/b]: nothing here reads or locks a simulation, so it is safe while a world is stepping. That is also what it is for -- predicting a collision that has not happened, or asking about geometry that was never added to a scene: a spawn check, a level tool, an AI probing a plan. For "what is in the scene right now", use [Box3DWorld]'s queries instead. Two conventions run through the whole class. [b]A primitive is spelled out in arguments[/b], as Box3D spells it: a sphere is a centre and a radius, a capsule is its two end-cap centres and a radius, a hull is a point cloud that gets hulled for you. [b]A proxy is the generic query shape[/b]: a point cloud plus a radius. One point with a radius is a sphere, two are a capsule, eight with radius 0 are a box, and any cloud is its own convex hull. At most 128 points. [b]Everything is in one frame: shape A's.[/b] Upstream runs the pair queries in A's frame and returns their points and normals there, so [code]transform_b[/code] is always B's pose [i]relative to A[/i], and a result has to be moved into world space by the caller. The warm-start caches upstream exposes are not bound: they only pay off across repeated calls with nearby poses, and a wrong one is a wrong answer, so each call here starts clean.

method.name: collide_capsule_and_sphere
method.description: The manifold between a capsule (A) and a sphere (B). Same result as [method collide_spheres].

method.name: collide_capsules
method.description: The manifold between two capsules. Same result as [method collide_spheres].

method.name: collide_hull_and_capsule
method.description: The manifold between a hull and a capsule. Same result as [method collide_spheres].

method.name: collide_hull_and_sphere
method.description: The manifold between the convex hull of [param points_a] and a sphere. Same result as [method collide_spheres].

method.name: collide_hulls
method.description: The manifold between two convex hulls. Same result as [method collide_spheres]. Both hulls are built for the call and freed before it returns.

method.name: collide_spheres
method.description: The manifold two spheres would produce if they met at these poses -- the narrow phase itself, run outside any world. Returns [code]normal[/code] ([Vector3]) and [code]points[/code] (an [Array] of [code]{ point, separation, triangle_index }[/code]). [b]Both are local to A[/b], not world space, and an empty [code]points[/code] means the shapes are apart. [param transform_b] is B's pose in A's frame. This is the question a spawn check asks: not "is there anything here" but "what would the contact look like".

method.name: collide_triangle_and_capsule
method.description: The manifold between a single triangle and a capsule, with the same triangle-first ordering as [method collide_triangle_and_sphere].

method.name: collide_triangle_and_hull
method.description: The manifold between a single triangle and a convex hull. [param triangle_flags] marks which of the triangle's edges are concave, as Box3D's mesh edge flags do; [code]0[/code] treats every edge as convex, which is right for a lone triangle. [param enable_speculative] keeps points that are close but not yet touching, as the solver does.

method.name: collide_triangle_and_sphere
method.description: The manifold between a single triangle and a sphere. [param triangle] is three points, already in A's frame, which is why it takes no transform of its own. [b]The normal points from the triangle towards the other shape[/b], which is the ordering the mesh narrow phase uses.

method.name: compute_capsule_aabb
method.description: The world-space [AABB] of the capsule described by [param center1], [param center2] and [param radius], posed by [param transform].

method.name: compute_capsule_mass
method.description: Mass properties of the capsule described by [param center1], [param center2] and [param radius] at [param density]. Same keys as [method compute_sphere_mass].

method.name: compute_hull_aabb
method.description: The world-space [AABB] of the convex hull of [param points], posed by [param transform].

method.name: compute_hull_mass
method.description: Mass properties of the convex hull of [param points] at [param density]. Same keys as [method compute_sphere_mass] -- the way to weigh a shape before deciding whether to build it.

method.name: compute_sphere_aabb
method.description: The world-space [AABB] of the sphere at [param center] with [param radius], posed by [param transform].

method.name: compute_sphere_mass
method.description: Mass properties of the sphere at [param center] with [param radius] at [param density]: [code]mass[/code] ([float]), [code]center[/code] ([Vector3]) and [code]inertia[/code] ([Basis]). The same three keys [method Box3DBody.get_mass_data] uses, so a computed tensor can be handed straight to [method Box3DBody.set_mass_data].

method.name: get_sweep_transform
method.description: The pose at [param time] along the sweep from [param from] to [param to], where [param time] is the fraction [method time_of_impact] reports. Rotation is interpolated as Box3D interpolates it, so this agrees with the impact the sweep found.

method.name: is_valid_ray
method.description: Whether a ray is well formed: finite origin and translation, and a [param max_fraction] Box3D accepts. Every ray cast here runs it first, so a bad ray is a clean miss rather than an assert -- call it yourself when you want to know [i]why[/i] a cast returned nothing.

method.name: overlap_capsule
method.description: [method overlap_sphere] against a capsule described by [param center1], [param center2] and [param radius].

method.name: overlap_hull
method.description: [method overlap_sphere] against the convex hull of [param points].

method.name: overlap_sphere
method.description: Whether the proxy described by [param proxy_points] and [param proxy_radius] overlaps the sphere at [param center] with [param radius], posed by [param transform]. [param transform] poses the [b]primitive[/b]; the proxy is already where its points say it is.

method.name: ray_cast_capsule
method.description: Casts a ray at the capsule described by [param center1], [param center2] and [param radius]. Same result as [method ray_cast_sphere], including the inside-is-a-hit rule.

method.name: ray_cast_hollow_sphere
method.description: [method ray_cast_sphere] against a [b]shell[/b] rather than a ball: a ray starting inside passes through the interior and hits the far wall, which is what a containment or dome test wants.

method.name: ray_cast_hull
method.description: Casts a ray at the convex hull of [param points]. The hull is built for the call and freed before it returns. Same result as [method ray_cast_sphere].

method.name: ray_cast_sphere
method.description: Casts a ray at the sphere at [param center] with [param radius], in the sphere's own frame. Returns [code]hit[/code] ([bool]), plus [code]position[/code], [code]normal[/code], [code]fraction[/code] and [code]iterations[/code]. A zero-length translation is a point query, and an origin [b]inside[/b] the sphere reports a hit at the origin with fraction 0 and a zero normal.

method.name: shape_cast
method.description: Sweeps proxy B, posed at [param transform_b], along [param translation_b] against a fixed proxy A, in A's frame. Returns the same [Dictionary] as [method ray_cast_sphere]. Touching at the start is a miss. This is the general form of the [code]shape_cast_*[/code] methods above, for when both shapes are point clouds.

method.name: shape_cast_capsule
method.description: [method shape_cast_sphere] against a capsule described by [param center1], [param center2] and [param radius].

method.name: shape_cast_hull
method.description: [method shape_cast_sphere] against the convex hull of [param points].

method.name: shape_cast_sphere
method.description: Sweeps the proxy described by [param proxy_points] and [param proxy_radius] along [param translation], against the sphere at [param center]. Returns the same [Dictionary] as [method ray_cast_sphere]. [b]Initial overlap is a miss[/b] here, the opposite of the ray casts: a sweep that starts touching reports nothing. [param can_encroach] lets a proxy with a radius close slightly further when it is already touching.

method.name: shape_distance
method.description: The closest points between two convex proxies, with B posed at [param transform_b] in A's frame. Returns [code]point_a[/code] and [code]point_b[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]normal[/code] ([Vector3]), [code]distance[/code] ([float]) and [code]iterations[/code] ([int]). A [code]distance[/code] of 0 means they overlap, and [code]normal[/code] is meaningless there -- that is upstream's overlap signal, so test the distance before trusting the normal. [param use_radii] accounts for each proxy's radius; turn it off to measure between the point clouds themselves.

method.name: time_of_impact
method.description: The first moment between 0 and [param max_fraction] at which two [b]sweeping[/b] proxies touch. Each sweep is given as its frame's start and end pose ([param from_a] to [param to_a], [param from_b] to [param to_b]), with the points in that frame. Returns [code]state[/code] (one of the [enum TOIState] values), [code]state_name[/code] ([String]), [code]fraction[/code] ([float]), [code]distance[/code] ([float]), [code]point[/code] and [code]normal[/code] ([Vector3]), plus three iteration counts for diagnostics. Feed [code]fraction[/code] to [method get_sweep_transform] to get the pose at the moment of impact. This is how a fast projectile is tested against a moving target without stepping either of them. Upstream warns that it uses a swept separating axis and can miss intermediate collisions that do not tunnel.

constants.constant: No result: the query did not run to a conclusion. Treat it as "do not act on this".
The solver could not converge on an impact time. Rare, and a signal to fall back on a simpler test rather than to trust the fraction.
The two shapes already overlap at the start of the sweep, so there is no impact time to find.
The shapes touch during the sweep. [code]fraction[/code] is when, and is the only state in which it means anything.
The shapes never touch over the whole sweep.
